slides: In the last lessons we learned the basic rules of the circle, and we practiced basic questions and harder ones. Now let's use these circle rules in some more involved questions.

slides.say: In fact, you already have the tools for most circle questions on the exam. The new questions just combine them in more steps.
We'll meet a few ideas that come back again and again in these questions. The first one is shaded areas. We'll ask which shape minus which shape gives the shaded part.
at: The first one is shaded areas

slides.say: The second one is a shape inside a circle, or a circle inside a shape. When a length depends on the radius, we'll write it using r.
at: The second one is a shape

slides.say: We'll also use quick exam ways, beside the math way. In the math way, we'll sometimes stop halfway and look at the choices. With plugging in numbers, we put a number instead of a letter. And with estimation, we rule out choices by their size. These ways are often faster, and they help even when we're not sure of the full solution.
at: stop halfway and look at the choices

slides.say: First, let's practise choosing the two areas. The order of subtraction depends on the picture.
Here the two radii are both two, with a right angle between them. We want the shaded segment between chord A B and the arc.
The quarter circle contains the triangle and the shaded segment. So take the whole quarter circle, then remove triangle A O B. What's left is the shaded segment.
The full circle has area pi times two squared, four pi. Ninety degrees is a quarter of the circle. Four pi divided by four is pi, so the quarter is pi.
The triangle is right, with legs of two. Its area is two times two, divided by two. That's two.
So the shaded area is pi minus two. We subtract the triangle because it's the piece inside the sector that we don't want.
Now the shaded parts are outside the circle but inside this triangle. The base is four, and the height is the radius, two. The angle at O is ninety degrees.
This time the whole triangle contains a quarter circle and the shaded parts. Take the triangle, then remove the quarter circle. The shaded parts are what remain.
The triangle's area is four times two, divided by two, which is four.
The radius is two again, so the quarter circle's area is pi, just as before.

So this shaded area is four minus pi. Same subtraction method, but the whole shape is different. First name the whole region. Then name the piece you remove. Don't always subtract in the same order. Now let's use this in the questions, and I'll see you in the next video.
